raw.assessment: Repeated three-compartment orders taking seven to nine minutes suggest existing routines approach the time target; mixed batches contain the longest orders. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. Missing-part reports and short-partition questions indicate possible fulfillment and interpretation failures; reports do not establish verified defect frequency. As a limiting observation, overlapping widths among first- and second-attempt insertions weaken a width-only explanation without excluding slot geometry or orientation. Combined timing cannot identify the main delay. These synthetic observations do not demonstrate pilot success.

openings.claim: Order-specific, pre-counted staging may reduce selection mistakes and switching effort.
openings.delta: Check component counts before insertion, retaining the final check and assembled delivery.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts and colors, staging reduces selection/checking time and content discrepancies; insertion time changes little. Savings disappear if staging merely relocates work.
openings.probe: Use six spare-board sample organizers covering three-, four-, and six-compartment layouts. Repeat matched mixed sequences with both workers, counterbalancing current and staged processes. Record selection, insertion, checking, packing, staging and reset time separately; audit contents against order slips. Include preparation labor and material costs.
assumptions: Reusable staging fits the existing bench.
Trials and adoption remain within the fixed delivery date, 500 initial cost and 0.40 added material cost per order; feasibility requires measurement.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement success.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with the selected layout and a recognizable short-partition silhouette.
openings.prediction: The specific diagram reduces short-partition placement questions and improves ordered-arrangement success without changing component geometry.
openings.probe: Randomly assign the ten participants five per diagram condition, using verified complete sample kits and matched layout difficulty. Record unaided success within ten minutes, placement errors and physical insertion failures separately. Treat results as exploratory, not proof of the 90% pilot target.
assumptions: Existing diagram material carries the replacement within cost limits.
Preparation fits available working time; partitions remain removable and ordered counts, colors, footprint and capacity are retained.

raw.assessment: The supplied observations leave selection errors, layout switching, insertion difficulty and instruction ambiguity unresolved. Neither opening establishes the pilot targets. Preserve existing parts, footprint, capacity, selected counts and colors, rearrangeability and delivery date; reject implementation exceeding either cost cap.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: use a reusable order-specific silhouette board as a spatial bill of materials. Workers fill every required position before assembly, then include a corresponding ordered-layout map identifying the short partition instead of the generic three-layout diagram.
openings.delta: Convert remembering a mixed collection into detecting empty or mismatched positions; carry the same part identities into customer instructions.
openings.prediction: On mixed-layout orders, selection/checking mistakes and customer uncertainty about the short partition decline without an offsetting increase in total workshop time.
openings.probe: Use a reusable spare-board prototype in matched mixed-layout trials with both workers, counterbalancing method order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; compare against an independently checked component list. Give five participants the new map and five the current diagram with matched layouts; count unaided ordered arrangements. Treat this small comparison as screening, then verify pilot completeness, median time and customer success.
assumptions: Existing part shapes are distinguishable on the board.
Reusable tooling plus map replacement can stay within 500 initially and 0.40 additional material per order.
Preparation and trials fit the fixed delivery schedule.

openings.claim: Insertion sequence may create temporary obstruction: a short partition that is easy to insert first becomes difficult or visually ambiguous after neighboring partitions are installed.
openings.delta: Test order-dependent accessibility without changing partition dimensions or making connections permanent.
openings.prediction: With identical parts and slots, short-first assembly reduces retries and insertion time; persistent difficulty independent of sequence weakens this explanation.
openings.probe: Within the combined 15-sample allowance, counterbalance short-first and short-last assembly across both workers and layouts. Track part/slot identity, retries and time; balance first use to limit wear confounding. Adopt sequence instructions only if total time improves and subsequent dismantling/rearrangement remains workable.
assumptions: A sequence change can be shown on the existing instruction sheet within both cost caps and the fixed schedule.

openings.claim: Pre-counted staging/silhouette positions may reduce selection errors and switching effort.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking improves, insertion unchanged; include preparation/reset labor.
openings.fit: Conditional: bench space, distinguishable shapes, global limits.
openings.probe: Both workers counterbalance matched current/staged mixed sequences on six samples across layouts/colors; time phases and independently audit contents.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout maps locating short partitions may improve comprehension; share staging/map identities.
openings.discriminator: Separate placement questions/errors from physical insertion failures.
openings.fit: Conditional: replace existing sheet within limits.
openings.probe: Randomize ten customers five per diagram, matching layouts and complete kits; measure ten-minute unaided success.

openings.discriminator: Identical parts/slots improve short-first versus short-last; sequence-independent difficulty weakens hypothesis.
openings.fit: Conditional: feasible sequences, removability, global limits.
openings.probe: Counterbalance workers/layouts/sequences and first-use wear; track identities, retries/time; check dismantling/rearrangement.
openings.uncertainty: Overlapping widths weaken width-only attribution; slot geometry/orientation remain possible.

lineage.reason: Checking and shared instruction identities preserved.

post_distill.decision: Screen within 15 samples total. Preserve assembled delivery, 30x20 footprint, capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors and deadline; enforce 500 initial/0.40 recurring caps. Synthetic evidence proves no target: verify 98% completeness, median <=8 minutes and 90% unaided success in the 60-unit pilot.
